1	# Runtime Checklist
2	
3	## Binary Selection
4	
5	- Prefer an installed `unity-cli` binary when it exists on `PATH` (the installer links it to `~/.local/bin/unity-cli`).
6	- If no binary is installed, run `scripts/install.sh` (macOS / Linux) or `scripts/install.ps1` (Windows, when published) instead of asking the user.
7	- Only inside a unity-cli source checkout, `cargo run -- <args>` is a development alternative.
8	
9	## Project Setup
10	
11	- `unity-cli setup` = binary check → `bridge install` → Editor `ping`; it prints one JSON report and exits non-zero until the Editor answers for this project.
12	- Tell the user before running it: it edits `Packages/manifest.json` and, when the project uses only the legacy Input Manager and the Editor is closed, sets `activeInputHandler: 2` (Both) in `ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset` so the Input System dependency does not block the Editor with a restart dialog. `bridge install` is idempotent (a second run leaves both files byte-identical).
13	- If the Editor was already open, it may show "enable the Input System backends? (restart)"; bridge commands time out until someone answers it. Close the Editor and rerun `setup --launch-editor` instead.
14	- `--launch-editor` starts the Unity Hub Editor recorded in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (`UNITY_EDITOR_PATH` overrides) and waits up to 900 s (`--wait-secs`).
15	- `editor.projectMatches: false` means another project's Editor owns the port; pass `--port`.
16	- `versionCheck.status: mismatch` (from `setup` or `system ping`) → `unity-cli bridge upgrade`, or update the CLI.
17	- Verify the binary with `unity-cli --version` before debugging higher-level workflows.
18	
19	## Instance Selection
20	
21	- Use `unity-cli system ping` when a single active target is expected.
22	- Use `unity-cli instances list` when multiple editors may be running.
23	- Prefer `--project-path <project>` (or running inside the project) to target one Editor; `AMBIGUOUS_EDITOR` lists candidates in `data.candidates`.
24	- Use `unity-cli instances set-active <host:port>` only after confirming the target is `up`.
25	
26	## Command Routing
27	
28	- The bootstrap-relevant typed subcommands are `system ping`, `scene create`, `instances list`, `instances set-active`. Use them when available. (`instances list` / `instances set-active` are local registry operations rather than bridge-tool wrappers.)
29	- The `reference *` family (`fetch`, `status`, `search`, `grep`, `view`, `find-symbol`, `diff`, `resolve-symbol-at`, `embed-build`, `embed-search`, `clean`) also has typed wrappers over the `reference_*` bridge tools — see the `unity-csharp-reference` skill. Beyond these, most bridge tools have no typed wrapper.
30	- For every tool without a typed wrapper, use `unity-cli raw <tool_name> --json '{...}'` (or its alias `unity-cli tool call <tool_name> --json '{...}'`). This is the primary invocation pattern, not a fallback — bridge tools such as `analyze_scene_contents`, `find_by_component`, `modify_component`, and `get_compilation_state` are all invoked this way.
31	- Discover tools with `unity-cli tool list --query <term> --compact`; add `--category <name>` (a `docs/tools.md` heading or slug such as `scenes`, `playback-testing`) and `--limit N` / `--offset N` to keep output small. Inspect a tool's expected JSON payload with `unity-cli tool schema <tool_name> --output json`.
32	- Use `--output json` when another tool or script will consume the result.
33	
34	## Connection Recovery
35	
36	- A failed `system ping` does not prove the Editor is closed. Run `unity-cli doctor --output json` (add `--project-path <dir>` outside the project) before any fallback such as hand-editing YAML.
37	- Act on the `diagnosis` code:
38	  - `SAFE_MODE` / `COMPILE_ERRORS`: the bridge is not loaded. Fix each `editorLog.compileErrors[]` entry (`file`, `line`, `code`) by editing the file directly, then let Unity recompile or restart the Editor.
39	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_INSTALLED`: run `unity-cli setup` (or `unity-cli bridge install`) to add `com.akiojin.unity-cli-bridge` to `Packages/manifest.json`.
40	  - `PORT_IN_USE`: `port.listenerPid` / `port.listenerProcess` hold the port. Stop it or change the bridge port and pass the same `--port`.
41	  - `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`: start the Editor for the project and wait for import to finish.
42	  - `SANDBOX_BLOCKED`: the local socket was denied. Retry in a permitted execution context according to the host's approval policy; do not bypass sandbox restrictions or conclude the Editor is missing. If reachability still cannot be verified, ask the user to confirm the running project and bridge connection before considering an offline fallback.
43	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_RESPONDING`: the Editor is still importing/compiling or the port differs from Project Settings > Unity CLI Bridge.
44	- Re-run `unity-cli doctor` until `diagnosis` is `OK`, then continue the workflow.
45	- An empty instance list or failed process probe inside a sandbox is also inconclusive. Confirm the project/host/port and the user's Editor state instead of treating restricted visibility as `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`.
46	- When the target Editor is reachable, never hand-edit serialized `.unity`, `.prefab`, or `.asset` YAML. Bridge operations keep serialized references, prefab overrides, and the live Editor state in sync.
47	- If recovery cannot restore the connection and offline work is appropriate, declare the fallback before editing: explain the verified limitation, affected files, alternative method, and how the result will be checked after reopening Unity. Without confirmation of an uncertain sandbox diagnosis, pause dependent edits. Do not silently substitute YAML edits for bridge calls.
48	
49	## CI Notes
50	
51	- Set `UNITY_CLI_HOST` and `UNITY_CLI_PORT` explicitly in CI.
52	- Keep JSON payloads quoted as a single shell argument.
53	- If connectivity fails in CI, report the resolved host and port before retrying.
54

1	# URP asset and visual verification workflow
2	
3	## Package and pipeline
4	
5	- Inspect `package_manager` `list` / `info` and the installed package API before
6	  choosing a version. Unity 2022.3 uses URP 14; Unity 6000.3 uses URP 17.3.
7	  Resolve the patch from the Editor's supported package information. Do not install
8	  another Editor's package or hardcode one patch for every project.
9	- Install with `package_manager` `{"action":"add","packageId":"com.unity.render-pipelines.universal@<compatible-version>"}`.
10	  Domain Reload may disconnect the bridge: wait and inspect state rather than
11	  blindly repeating the install. Read the actual installed version afterward.
12	- For an existing URP Asset, inspect its renderer and preserve Renderer Features.
13	  For a new asset use `UniversalRenderPipelineAsset.Create(rendererData)` with a
14	  `UniversalRendererData`. Initialize its post-processing resources using the
15	  installed package's default `PostProcessData` and Editor resource reloader;
16	  merely constructing a blank ScriptableObject may leave shaders unassigned.
17	  Save Renderer and pipeline as separate `.asset` files with `AssetDatabase`.
18	- `GraphicsSettings.defaultRenderPipeline` chooses the default. A non-null
19	  `QualitySettings.renderPipeline` overrides it. Inspect all Quality levels before
20	  choosing whether to replace their overrides; preserve the active level. Assign
21	  only the levels included in the request and report that scope.
22	- Enable HDR on the pipeline and Camera for a Bloom test with HDR emission.
23	  For a Built-in scene, incompatible materials can render pink; use a separate
24	  URP-compatible test material rather than automatically converting the project.
25	
26	## Persistent Volume and Camera
27	
28	Use `editor eval --mode statements` for small synchronous Editor API operations.
29	URP namespaces are not implicit; use fully qualified names. Evaluate only after
30	the package has compiled. Check `state:"completed"` and diagnostics, even if the
31	CLI exit code is zero. Give mutations unique `--request-id` values; query
32	`editor eval-status` after a timeout before deciding to retry.
33	
34	Create a `UnityEngine.Rendering.VolumeProfile` asset and add
35	`UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal.Bloom` via `profile.Add<T>(true)`. Add the returned
36	component to the profile asset with `AssetDatabase.AddObjectToAsset`; mark both
37	dirty and save. Do the same for `ColorAdjustments` when requested. On an existing
38	profile use `TryGet<T>` first; do not duplicate overrides or overwrite user values.
39	
40	For Bloom, set `active`, `intensity.overrideState`, `intensity.value`,
41	`threshold.overrideState` and `threshold.value`. A test value such as intensity 2
42	and threshold 1 needs a visible subject brighter than threshold. Color Adjustments
43	can use `postExposure.Override(...)`; avoid changing it during a Bloom-only A/B
44	comparison. Keep all other variables fixed.
45	
46	Add or reuse a `UnityEngine.Rendering.Volume` on the intended GameObject:
47	`isGlobal = true`, nonzero `weight`, and `sharedProfile = savedProfile`. Use a
48	deliberate priority when other volumes overlap. Accessing `volume.profile` may
49	create an instance; edit `sharedProfile` for content that must persist.
50	
51	On the target Camera, add or reuse `UniversalAdditionalCameraData`, enable
52	`renderPostProcessing`, and include the Volume object's layer in `volumeLayerMask`.
53	Check camera stacking and renderer selection if the scene uses multiple cameras.
54	Mark changed objects dirty, mark the scene dirty and save it through Editor APIs.
55	
56	## Before/after evidence
57	
58	1. Record paths and GUIDs for the pipeline, renderer and profile. Capture their
59	   assignment and values plus the active Camera and Quality level in JSON.
60	2. Save a stationary test scene. Repository E2E fixtures belong under
61	   `Assets/Scenes/Generated/E2E/`. Use the same scene for both images; do not
62	   compare a Built-in baseline with different geometry to a URP result.
63	3. Set only Bloom intensity to zero (or disable that override), enter Play, wait
64	   for stable rendered frames, and call `capture_screenshot` in `game` mode with
65	   fixed width/height and `osFallback:false`. Keep the returned image path.
66	4. Set the intended Bloom intensity, let frames settle and capture again. Inspect
67	   both images: the bright subject should gain a visible glow while framing stays
68	   fixed. A byte/hash difference alone could be animation or a capture artifact.
69	5. Read console errors and the live values. Stop Play, restore the desired saved
70	   value, save assets/scene, reload and confirm assignments and overrides survive.
71	   Include the assets and both images with the verification report.
72	
73	If the images look identical, inspect in this order: effective Quality/Graphics
74	pipeline, Camera `renderPostProcessing`, assigned renderer/post-processing
75	resources, Volume layer mask and weight/priority, active override flags and
76	threshold versus subject brightness. Confirm Game capture succeeded; an OS or
77	Scene-view capture does not demonstrate the target Camera's post-processing.
78	
79	## API sources
80	
81	- Unity's URP package API, not third-party plugin skill text, defines the types:
82	  `UniversalRenderPipelineAsset`, `UniversalRendererData`, `PostProcessData`,
83	  `UniversalAdditionalCameraData`, `VolumeProfile`, `Bloom`, `ColorAdjustments`.
84	- Read installed package sources when an API differs between URP 14 and 17.
85	  Rendering resources and RenderGraph internals should not be guessed or replaced
86	  with custom reflection-based bridge extensions.
